backlog.title: Rev 2 Streaming Delta Bugfix — Output Reliability Recovery
backlog.description: Fix the 8 validated defects in the Rev 2 streaming delta (PRD h2.0): one critical silent-output-death bug (rejected-final session freeze), three major sequencing bugs (post-cancel suppression, frozen-commit separator, missing partial-path listening gate), four minor robustness bugs (empty-line control hang, unknown config tables, 5s stop-after-cancel drain, guard-induced rewind churn). All fixes are confined to voice_typing/{streaming,daemon,config,textproc}.py plus fast double-based tests; no new dependencies, no CUDA suites required. Research findings for downstream agents live in plan/007_cfc245548aec/bugfix/001_23df36029e8d/architecture/ (system_context.md, streaming_engine.md, daemon_flow.md, config_tests_docs.md, external_deps.md).

milestones.title: Critical & major streaming state-machine fixes (BUG-001..BUG-004)
milestones.description: Restore correct engine/daemon sequencing: rejected finals must not kill the session's output, the re-said sentence after Backspace-cancel must stream live, frozen commits must separate words, and stale partials must never type while toggled off. Engine work is sequenced (shared resume seam, then frozen-path space, then case-insensitive extends) to avoid conflicts in streaming.py.

tasks.title: BUG-001: Scope the rejected-final freeze to the utterance (recover typed output after a blocklist/min_chars rejection)
tasks.description: A single rejected final currently freezes StreamingOutput session-class (daemon.py:1154) — every later utterance of the armed session types nothing until re-arm. Introduce an explicit engine resume seam that a session-class rejected-final freeze does not survive, wire it to the daemon's next-speech signal, and add the user-visible rejection cue. Per PRD h2.1/h3.0 and h2.5; the fix must NOT be a naive session=False retag (daemon.py:1150-1153 comment explains why: reset_boundary() fires on the next line and stray late partials must stay inert).

The in-code comment at daemon.py:1150-1153 pins a test asserting frozen==True across the rejected-final sequence and forbids retagging to per-utterance.

Test doubles: fake backend with type_text/press_backspace + fake feedback with update_partial (patterns in tests/test_streaming_freeze.py, tests/test_streaming_core.py).

LOGIC: Implement the PRD h2.5 fix 'explicit unfreeze at the next utterance's first partial/speech': add ONE explicit engine resume API (e.g. resume()) that clears _suppressed and lifts ONLY a rejected-final freeze — backend-failure session freezes (_safe_type/_safe_backspace, streaming.py:472/:485) must still survive every boundary; keep freeze() promote-only semantics. Track the freeze REASON/class so resume() cannot lift a backend-failure freeze. Additionally: when the daemon resets the boundary after a rejected final, absorb the frozen tail into _committed (same rstrip-join discipline as commit()'s frozen path) so guards/context/mirror stay truthful — today reset_boundary() :221 orphans the on-screen fragment from the checkpoint. tasks.title: BUG-002: Restore live streaming for the re-said sentence after Backspace-cancel
tasks.description: daemon.cancel() sets engine _suppressed until 'the next utterance boundary', but the cancelled sentinel final is dropped at on_final's suppression branch before any reset_boundary() fires — so every partial of the re-said sentence is mirror-only until its commit (Rev 1 append-only degradation). Lift the suppression at the next utterance START (speech event), per PRD h2.2/h3.1 and h2.5.

tasks.title: BUG-003: Frozen commit omits the trailing space (glued words)
tasks.description: commit()'s frozen-absorb path (streaming.py:415-425) joins committed+tail without typing the append_space separator; after the daemon's post-commit reset_boundary lifts the user-keypress freeze, the next utterance's first word glues onto the tail. PRD h2.2/h3.2 + h2.5: append the trailing space in the frozen-absorb path.

milestones.title: Minor robustness fixes (BUG-005..BUG-008)
milestones.description: Control-socket empty-line hang, unknown config-table rejection, immediate stop after cancel, and case-insensitive extend matching. tasks.title: BUG-005: Control socket — reply to empty request lines
tasks.description: ControlServer._handle silently skips empty lines (daemon.py:2453-2454), hanging clients forever on a socket with no read timeout. Reply with the malformed-JSON error shape instead. PRD h2.3/h3.4 + h2.5.

subtasks.title: Daemon: empty-line request gets a malformed-JSON error reply
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: plan/007_cfc245548aec/bugfix/001_23df36029e8d/architecture/daemon_flow.md — ControlServer._handle (daemon.py:2444) strips each line and runs 'if not line: continue' (:2453-2454, comment: 'empty line -> skip (no response)'); malformed JSON is answered {'ok': False, 'error': 'malformed JSON: <exc>'} at :2496-2497; the control socket has NO read timeout (voice_typing/ctl.py send_command + AGENTS.md hazard table) — which is exactly why silence hangs clients.
2. INPUT: ControlServer._handle/_dispatch as-is; round-trip test fixtures in tests/test_control_socket.py (test_round_trip_status :190 pattern uses an in-process ControlServer over a real socketpair/unix socket).
3. LOGIC: PRD h2.3/h3.4 + h2.5: replace the silent continue with a reply in the SAME error shape, e.g. {'ok': False, 'error': 'malformed JSON: empty request line'}; keep serving subsequent lines on the same connection (do not close/break). Write the failing test FIRST at ROUND-TRIP level (the continue lives in _handle, not _dispatch): one connection sends an empty line (b'\n') and a whitespace-only line (b'   \n'), then a valid status request — each empty line must yield exactly one JSON error reply line and the status must still answer. No live daemon, no voicectl; in-process ControlServer only.
4. OUTPUT: fixed _handle + green round-trip test.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the ControlServer class docstring behavior table (daemon.py ~:2338, 'malformed JSON -> ...' row) to document the empty-line reply; check README 'Logs, status, stopping' (:339) and update ONLY if it documents request framing.

tasks.title: BUG-007: Stop immediately after a Backspace-cancel
tasks.description: The cancelled sentinel's early return in on_final skips _final_pending=False, so stop-after-cancel takes a pointless ~5s graceful-drain abort for a final that can never come. PRD h2.3/h3.6 + h2.5.

subtasks.title: Daemon: clear _final_pending when the cancelled sentinel is consumed
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: plan/007_cfc245548aec/bugfix/001_23df36029e8d/architecture/daemon_flow.md — on_final's suppression branch (daemon.py:1130-1137) returns BEFORE 'self._final_pending = False' (:1165); _request_stop (:1391) drains iff host is not None AND _text_in_flight.is_set() AND _final_pending — after a cancel all three hold, so stop waits the _DRAIN_TIMEOUT_S=5.0 watchdog (:149, timer at :1644) for a final whose audio was discarded.
2. INPUT: The suppression branch as reworked by P1.M1.T2.S2; cancel() (:1603) and _reset_stream_after_cancel (:1437); existing mocked drain tests in tests/test_daemon.py (29 per ACCEPTANCE row 10) for assertion style.
3. LOGIC: PRD h2.3/h3.6 + h2.5: clear _final_pending exactly when the cancelled sentinel is consumed (inside the suppression branch when consume_cancel_mark() returns True) — NOT unconditionally in cancel(), so a racing REAL final dropped by the same window cannot leave a stale pending flag either way; the sentinel closes the window, and only then is nothing pending. Do not change _request_stop's condition itself. Write the failing test FIRST (doubles only): arm; d._touch_speech() (flags the in-flight utterance); d.cancel(); then d._request_stop() -> the IMMEDIATE branch runs (disarm without _begin_drain — assert no drain timer / no watchdog arming, mirroring existing drain tests' style). Mock recorder with _StubRecorder/_FakeHost(consume_cancel_mark); no CUDA.
4. OUTPUT: immediate stop-after-cancel + green daemon test.
5. DOCS: none — no user-facing surface change.

tasks.title: BUG-008: Case-insensitive prefix matching in the EXTEND path
tasks.description: on_partial's EXTEND test is case-sensitive (streaming.py:328) while the casing guard lowercases fresh mid-sentence fragments, so capitalized decoder partials can never extend the guarded tail — every cycle becomes a rate-limited full rewind. PRD h2.3/h3.7 + h2.5.

subtasks.title: Engine: normalize case for the extend comparison only
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: plan/007_cfc245548aec/bugfix/001_23df36029e8d/architecture/streaming_engine.md — the EXTEND test 'if self._tail and text.startswith(self._tail)' (streaming.py:328) is case-sensitive, but textproc.apply_streaming_guards (textproc.py:107-134, rule (a)) lowercases the first cased character of a fresh mid-sentence fragment (committed not ending ./!?), so the guarded tail ('the quick') never prefix-matches the decoder's capitalized partials ('The quick brown...') -> full rewind+retype each cycle, throttled only by the 300ms rate limiter. commit()'s extend branch uses the same startswith pattern (~:417).
2. INPUT: StreamingOutput.on_partial EXTEND/REVISE branches (as they exist after P1.M1.T1.S1/P1.M1.T2.S1 landed); _guard_context_delta (:463); fake backend recording type_text/press_backspace calls.
3. LOGIC: PRD h2.5 recommendation: normalize case for the prefix COMPARISON ONLY — typed output keeps the decoder's casing; delta = text[len(self._tail):] guarded as today. Use a LENGTH-PRESERVING normalization (beware casefold changing lengths, e.g. 'İ'; if the lowered prefix slice does not match by length, fall back to the REVISE path). Mirror the same comparison in commit()'s extend branch only if it keeps commit behavior consistent. Write the failing test FIRST from the PRD h3.7 repro: commit('and then he said'); reset_boundary(); partials 'Hello there' -> type 'hello there' (guarded); 'Hello there friend' -> EXTEND types ' friend' with ZERO press_backspace calls; 'Hello there friend how' -> EXTEND again; assert no full rewinds after the first cycle. Verify: timeout 600 uv run pytest tests/test_streaming_core.py tests/test_textproc.py -q.
4. OUTPUT: case-insensitive extends + green tests.
5. DOCS: none — internal flicker fix; README §Streaming dictation already promises delta typing.
